_comment: What a run report contains, named once and checked from both sides.
The python emitter writes this document and the dashboard's TypeScript
declares its shape, and until this file existed the two could drift in
silence: a renamed field turned into blank cells in a published table,
with nothing failing anywhere. tests/test_schema.py and
dashboard/test/schema.test.ts both read this file and both check the same
committed report, so a rename has to be made in three places or it fails.
Required fields only. A field that is genuinely absent on some rows --
vendorFiles, differences -- is not listed, because a contract that lies
about what is optional is worse than none.
//severities: Worst first; the order is the ranking a queue is sorted by. 'verification' was two categories until schema 3, 'problem' and 'review', and they are one because both end in the same place: somebody reading the row and deciding.
//unmatchedSignOffs: Per check, the sign-offs whose key matches no row the run produced -- a calibration file asset-management no longer carries, a deployment renumbered out of a sheet. Every check has an entry, empty when nothing is orphaned.
//comparedWith: The ref this run was measured against, or null. A comparison is published beside the report only when a run was given a baseline, so this is what says whether there is one to fetch. Always written: null means there is none, and the field being absent means the run predates it.
//parameters: What produced the numbers: the commit of this repository, whether it was dirty, and the libraries that parsed the files. Comparison is exact to the last digit, so the versions are part of the answer.
//source: A repository at a commit. The clone's path is deliberately absent -- it describes a machine, not the data.
//summary: Every category, plus verified (agreed plus cleared) and considered (the rows this check could judge at all, which is total less excluded). Schema 2 also carried attention, the count waiting on a person; that is now the verification category itself.
//row: On every row of every check. finding is what the checks found; severity is the category, which a sign-off changes and finding does not.
//rows: Per check, on top of the four above. hitlKey is the line a sign-off writes to, settled by the run rather than rebuilt in a browser.
//optional: Written only where the run has something to say. rawAssetID is the asset a mismatching raw serial belongs to, where it could be placed; rawFilesTried and rawAttemptedAt are what the archive was asked for, so a row with no serial says which files were read.
